knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/problem:
Express the following as a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
2\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}\right)\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}\right)
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
2\sin x\cos x &=\left[2\sin x\cos x\right] \\ &=\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{8\pi}{9}$. The result is

$$
\sin\left(\frac{8\pi}{9}\right) .
$$
